title: Yogurt takes meeting notes on your computer, without joining the call
friendlyTitle: Yogurt writes meeting notes on your computer, and does not join the call
summary: Frigade released Yogurt, a free open-source app for private AI meeting notes. It records the call from your computer and does not add a bot to the meeting. Downloads cover Apple-silicon Mac, Windows, and Linux. The project lists local speech and language models, and it asks for 8 GB of memory. The license is MIT. The latest release on the page is 0.3.5, dated 11 November.
friendlySummary: Yogurt is a free, open-source app for meeting notes. It records from your computer. It does not add a bot to the meeting. You can download it for a recent Apple-silicon Mac, Windows, or Linux. It uses local speech and language models, and it needs 8 GB of memory. The latest release is 0.3.5, from 11 November.
whyItMatters: A notes bot in the call is visible, and the audio often leaves the room. Yogurt is the other design: the app sits with you, and the notes are meant to stay on the machine. That is useful for a client call you cannot invite a bot into. It is new, at 173 stars, and it is not a hosted workspace. If you need shared team memory, this is not that product.
